newsitem.title: USA: Bay State says natgas liquid storage delayed.
newsitem.headline: Bay State says natgas liquid storage delayed.

text.p: Bay State Gas Co said on Friday a liquified natural gas storage facility in the northeastern United States is expected to be delayed, since the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission plans to supplement an environmental impact statement.

"We were surprised and disappointed with FERC's action because it will almost certainly delay the project by one year," Dwight Curley, president of Bay State Co's Granite State unit, said in a statement.
Final regulatory approvals are now expected in mid-1997.
Bay State representatives were not immediately available for comment or to say what city the site will be located.
Prior to the FERC order, the project was on schedule to begin construction this fall, in order to have the 580,000 barrel, US $50 million facility in operation beginning in November 1998.
The matter was pending before the agency since November 1994, Bay State said.
Bay State said it will comply with FERC's additional request for a more intensive site analysis and will continue to develop the project on the fastest practical timetable.

The project recently received unanimous approval from Maine and New Hampshire utility regulators and the Maine Department of Environmental Protection has issued a draft order finding that the projectwill not hurt the environment, Bay State said.
